_comment: Governed CODING CONVENTIONS consumed by claude_coder.conventions (issue #6, product-owner decision 2026-09-22). Each entry authorizes ONE value on ONE descriptor axis for a fact whose own source-confirmed evidence matches applies_when. Expressed in descriptor grammar (axis/value) and in what the record documents (regexes) -- NEVER a medical code (guarded by tests/test_conventions.py). Every entry MUST cite its authority with issue/date; verification_status records what was checked against the source and any DISSENT among authorities, so a reviewer sees a convention as a documented choice, never as settled fact. A convention never overrides a value the record itself states; it fills only an axis the record is silent on, and every use is written into the line's audit record.

conventions.authority: AMA CPT Assistant, March 2020 p.14 (Surgery/Musculoskeletal System, Q3) as corrected by the April 2020 erratum (p.8), referencing July 2019 p.5: debridement/debulking of a diseased Achilles tendon is reported with the secondary-repair Achilles descriptor, not an unlisted or muscle/fascia debridement descriptor; AHA Coding Clinic for HCPCS (as relayed in Becker's ASC 'Surgery Center Coding Guidance: Haglund's Deformity'): Achilles detachment/debridement/reattachment with calcaneal spur removal is captured by the secondary-repair Achilles descriptor; AOFAS coding guidance (as relayed in AAPC Orthopedic Coding Alert): 'Achilles tendon debridement and repair for tendonosis' -> the secondary-repair Achilles descriptor; AAPC coding-forum consensus (2024, citing CPT Assistant 24 May 2024 for the calcaneal ostectomy line): calcaneal ostectomy plus the secondary-repair Achilles descriptor for Achilles debridement due to tendonitis.
conventions.verification_status: verified 2026-09-22 against the public summaries of the sources above (the CPT Assistant and AMA CPT Knowledge Base full texts are paywalled: AMA KB entries 2017-01-09 'Should [the secondary-repair Achilles descriptor] be reported for a simple repair of a chronic Achilles tear (re-tear)...' and 2020-05-28 'When using the secondary repair [descriptor], does the descriptor mean the Achilles tendon...' were not readable). AUTHORITIES DISAGREE -- see dissent.
conventions.dissent: AOFAS guidance (via AAPC Orthopedic Coding Alert 'Could Be Best Choice for Non-Ruptured Tendon'): for debridement of INSERTIONAL Achilles tendinitis with repair (suture anchor vs bony trough) it names the TENOLYSIS leg/ankle descriptor, not the secondary-repair descriptor. AMA CPT Knowledge Base (via Becker's ASC): calcaneal ostectomy plus, for tendon work beyond exposure, the FOOT flexor-tendon repair descriptor. NYSPMA (2017): the PRIMARY-repair Achilles descriptor plus the calcaneal spur ostectomy descriptor. This entry follows the CPT Assistant / Coding Clinic / AOFAS-tendonosis position because it is the most-cited and most recent; the product owner may disable it or adopt a dissenting position by editing this file, never by changing code.
conventions.rationale: The primary-repair family in this descriptor set is defined on a RUPTURED tendon. A tendon that is debrided and reattached with no rupture documented does not satisfy that descriptor, and the record never literally states 'secondary'; the cited convention reports such a reattachment with the secondary-repair descriptor. Scoped to the Achilles family by candidate descriptor because that is the family the cited guidance addresses.

claim_controls.authority: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2026, Section I.B.4 (codes that describe symptoms and signs are acceptable for reporting when a related definitive diagnosis has not been established by the provider) and Section I.B.5 (signs and symptoms that are associated routinely with a disease process should not be assigned as additional codes, unless otherwise instructed by the classification)
claim_controls._how: a released diagnosis whose ICD-10-CM code is reached in the SNOMED CT -> ICD-10-CM map ONLY from concepts tagged (finding) is a sign/symptom code; it is not additionally reported when another released diagnosis, reached from (disorder) concepts, names a site the SNOMED body-structure graph relates to the symptom's site (same, or ancestor/descendant) with no contradicting laterality. Sites come from the codes' own descriptors (governed anatomy phrases) and the facts' typed anatomy; nothing is inferred from wording alone
claim_controls._why: designated operative note, third live run: the second reading surfaced the chief complaint ('pain in <site>') as its own diagnosis and it released beside three definitive diagnoses of that site; a coder would not report it
claim_controls._share_why: a code's mapped source concepts are counted by SNOMED semantic tag; a symptom code such as a localized-pain code is reached overwhelmingly from (finding) concepts (measured on the US 2026-03 edition: 'pain in <site>' codes 65-100% finding), a disease code overwhelmingly from (disorder) concepts; 0.6 leaves a genuinely mixed profile unclassified, which keeps the code reported (fail-open toward reporting, never toward silent removal)

claim_controls.authority: AMA CPT Assistant, March 2020 p.14 (Surgery/Musculoskeletal System, Q3) as corrected by the April 2020 erratum (p.8), referencing July 2019 p.5: debridement/debulking of a diseased Achilles tendon is reported with the secondary-repair Achilles descriptor, not with an unlisted, muscle/fascia debridement or separate tendon-excision descriptor; NCCI Policy Manual Ch. I (services integral to the primary procedure are not separately reportable)
claim_controls._why: designated operative note, fourth live run: the tendon debridement resolved to a separate tendon-lesion excision code beside the secondary-repair code already reporting the same Achilles work; the same authority the pack's sequence-qualifier convention cites says the debridement IS the secondary repair -- so the released component is excluded, never the parent
claim_controls._scope_why: scoped to a released parent whose descriptor is the secondary-repair Achilles code, and to a component whose own confirmed evidence documents debridement/debulking or removal of abnormal tendon tissue (no rupture documented) in the same operative episode -- the exact clinical situation the cited guidance addresses
